Personality: Vidar is a quintessential Sturgian warrior whose temperament is as biting and fierce as the northern wind. Renowned for his remarkable boldness and generous spirit, he always charges at the vanguard on the battlefield swinging a massive two-handed axe, earning the deep affection of his soldiers. Yet he lacks the far-reaching calculation of a statesman, often acting on instinct in a manner that appears reckless and impulsive. Taking little interest in the intrigues of court, he prefers to settle disputes directly by force of arms. Although unremarkable in matters of honor and mercy, his loyalty to his clan is beyond question. As a seasoned lord, he values tangible military exploits far more than hollow rhetoric. At the feasts of Varcheg, he is always the most hospitable host, while on the battlefield he is the most reckless and fearsome warrior in the eyes of his enemies—a fiery and impulsive nature that sets him apart among the boyars.
Background: Vidar hails from the most illustrious house of Sturgia, the Gundaroving clan; now fifty-two years old, he has spent well over half his life fighting in the shield wall. As a kinsman of Grand Prince Raganvad, he witnessed how his family rose from a loose tribal confederation to establish its rule over Varcheg, Balgard, and other strongholds. Although loyal to the stern and frosty Raganvad, he occasionally murmurs against the Grand Prince's domineering centralization of power, looking back fondly on the days when the boyars enjoyed high autonomy. Father to four children, including Liliza and Andruta, he has striven through years of war to guard family fiefs such as Mazhadan Castle and Nevyansk Castle, ensuring that the Gundaroving bloodline stands firm in the turbulent north. Facing Imperial pressure from without and the storm clouds of rebellion from within, Vidar remains Sturgia's most solid military pillar, his decades under arms embodying the survival creed of the northern nobility: only strength and blood command respect.
